title: Vaikka aikoivat itse olla yhteydessä
subtitle: Even though they intended to be in touch themselves

blocks.text: You have kun, koska, jos from Lesson 22 — timing, cause, condition. There's one more connector family reviewers reach for constantly: contrast. Vaikka ('although/even if') and its cousins kuitenkin and silti ('however/still') let a reviewer admit something positive right before undercutting it.

blocks.translation: Even though they intended to be in touch themselves.

blocks.title: Fairness through contrast
blocks.text: A review that says only good things or only bad things can feel one-sided. Vaikka, kuitenkin, and silti are the words that let a reviewer sound balanced and credible — 'the price was fine, but the wait was long' — even inside an otherwise harsh complaint. Watch for these words whenever a review pivots mid-sentence.

blocks.content: {Vaikka|grammar|conjunction|although/even if} introduces a fact that doesn't stop the main point from being true. Vaikka aikoivat itse olla yhteydessä, piti itse olla yhteydessä — 'even though they intended to be in touch themselves, [I] had to be in touch myself [instead]'. It works exactly like English 'although' or 'even if', sitting at the front of its clause.

items.fi: {Vaikka|grammar|conjunction|even though} hinta oli korkea, palvelu oli hyvää.
items.en: Even though the price was high, the service was good.

items.fi: Piti itse olla yhteydessä, {vaikka|grammar|conjunction|even though} aikoivat itse olla.
items.en: I had to be in touch myself, even though they intended to be in touch themselves.

blocks.content: Unlike vaikka, {kuitenkin|grammar|contrast adverb|however/nevertheless} and {silti|grammar|contrast adverb|still/nonetheless} don't need to sit at the front — they slot into the middle of a sentence and pivot it, exactly like English 'however' or 'still'. Muistivat kuitenkin laskuttaa täysmääräisesti — 'they nevertheless remembered to bill in full' — landing right after a run of apologetic-sounding sentences.

items.fi: Pahoittelivat tilannetta, mutta muistivat {kuitenkin|grammar|contrast adverb|nevertheless} laskuttaa täysmääräisesti.
items.en: They apologised for the situation, but nevertheless remembered to bill in full.
The price was high. I still recommend it.

blocks.text: Piece 3 — Stacking vaikka with what you already know

blocks.title: Vaikka combines naturally with earlier lessons
blocks.text: Vaikka often introduces a clause built from grammar you already own — a conditional (Lesson 5), a perfect (Lesson 23), or simply oli. Älä usko, vaikka he väittävät vastaan — 'don't believe it, even if they claim otherwise' — reuses Lesson 15's älä imperative right alongside vaikka.

items.fi: Älä usko, {vaikka|grammar|conjunction|even if} he väittävät vastaan.
items.en: Don't believe it, even if they claim otherwise.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Were they in touch with you?

lines.speaker: B
lines.fi: Eivät, vaikka aikoivat itse olla yhteydessä. Jouduin soittamaan itse.
lines.en: No, even though they intended to be in touch themselves. I had to call myself.

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: No. They nevertheless remembered to bill in full.

blocks.title: Paul Noble Rule
blocks.text: Vaikka opens a clause the same way kun/koska/jos do (Lesson 22) — front position, then the rest follows. Kuitenkin and silti are more flexible, sliding into a sentence wherever the pivot needs to land. Spot any of these three, and you know a contrast is coming, even before you've read what it is.

blocks.content: Vaikka: VAIK-ka (the 'vai' rhymes with English 'my', double k held). Kuitenkin: KUI-ten-kin (three syllables, the 'ui' glides). Silti: SIL-ti (short, crisp, two syllables).

blocks.title: What you now own
items: vaikka — although/even if, opening a contrast clause just like kun/koska/jos
kuitenkin and silti — however/still, pivoting mid-sentence rather than opening a clause
you can now read the fairness-signaling pivots reviewers use throughout the corpus
you can combine vaikka with earlier grammar — the imperative, the conditional, the perfect
your connector toolkit is now complete: kun, koska, jos (Lesson 22) plus vaikka, kuitenkin, silti (this lesson)
